reason: The probe wrote newline-delimited JSON (`JSON.stringify({id,method,params}) + '\n'`) to \\.\pipe\pidesktop-codex-ipc. The bridge's own receiver (installed cn.star.turnloom-bridge main.js, startPipeServer, lines 2094-2140) reads a 4-byte UInt32LE length prefix followed by a JSON frame, and ignores any frame whose `type` is not "request". A newline-delimited frame makes readUInt32LE(0) interpret the first 4 bytes of the JSON text as an enormous length, so the receiver waits forever and never replies. The observed timeout is therefore a protocol mismatch produced by the probe, not evidence about host responsiveness.

protocolFactsReadOnly.requiredEnvelope: lines 2117-2119: message.type must equal "request"; response carries type:"response", requestId, method, resultType

hostControlPathEvidence.conclusion: The app-facing host-control path is genuinely blocked: the pipe server answers in single-digit milliseconds, but every pi.desktop.invoke call fails with 'Plugin host process is no longer active'. This reproduces the same error the repairing session saw on two real POST /api/send attempts, using only read-only operations and without touching any real session, task or approval.
